## What it is

The Identification and Authentication policy states what the organization requires for identification and authentication and who is accountable for it. It meets [IA-1](/controls/ia/ia-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 22 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which multi-factor methods are accepted, and which are phishing-resistant enough for privileged access? | [IA-2(1)](/controls/ia/ia-2/#ia-2.1), [IA-2(2)](/controls/ia/ia-2/#ia-2.2), [IA-2(8)](/controls/ia/ia-2/#ia-2.8) | FIDO2 security keys, platform authenticators or PKI smart cards for privileged users; authenticator apps with number matching as a minimum for everyone else. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which identity provider authenticates users, and which systems may keep local accounts? | [IA-2](/controls/ia/ia-2/), [IA-8](/controls/ia/ia-8/) | One organization identity provider for all users; local accounts only for break-glass and service use, recorded in the security plan. | Chief Information Security Officer |

Record your values in the [Identification and Authentication decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/ia/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet IA-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the IA-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Identification and Authentication, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (IA-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (IA-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (IA-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (IA-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (IA-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (IA-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (IA-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (IA-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the identification and authentication policy is to be disseminated</span>. (IA-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the identification and authentication procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (IA-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Identification and authentication (organizational users) (IA-2)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system uniquely identifies and authenticates organizational users. (IA-2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system associates that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users. (IA-2)

#### Multi-factor authentication to privileged accounts (IA-2(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts. (IA-2(1))

#### Multi-factor authentication to non-privileged accounts (IA-2(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts. (IA-2(2))

#### Access to accounts: replay resistant (IA-2(8))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: privileged accounts; non-privileged accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: privileged accounts and non-privileged accounts</span></span>. (IA-2(8))

#### Acceptance of PIV credentials (IA-2(12))

:::note[Guidance]
Personal Identity Verification (PIV) is the U.S. federal smart card credential. An organization outside the federal government meets this enhancement where it relies on PIV or PIV-interoperable credentials; if it uses none, record the enhancement as not applicable in the system security plan with that reason.
:::

- Where the organization issues or relies on Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system accepts and electronically verifies them. (IA-2(12))

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

Federal employees and contractors are issued PIV credentials under Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and [FIPS 201-3](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/201-3/final), Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors (January 2022).

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system accepts and electronically verifies PIV credentials for organizational users. (IA-2(12))

</div>

#### Device identification and authentication (IA-3)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system uniquely identifies and authenticates <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: devices and/or types of devices to be uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a connection <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all organization-managed endpoints, servers and network devices</span></span> before establishing a <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: local; remote; network <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: remote and network</span></span> connection. (IA-3)

#### Identifier management (IA-4)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall assign an individual, group, role, service or device identifier only with authorization from <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles from whom authorization must be received to assign an identifier <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner, through the approved access request</span></span>. (IA-4a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall select an identifier that identifies the individual, group, role, service or device. (IA-4b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall assign the identifier to the intended individual, group, role, service or device. (IA-4c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall prevent reuse of identifiers for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: a time period for preventing reuse of identifiers <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least two years</span></span>. (IA-4d)

#### Identify user status (IA-4(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall manage individual identifiers so that each individual is uniquely identified as <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: characteristics used to identify individual status <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: employee, contractor, or foreign national</span></span>. (IA-4(4))

#### Authenticator management (IA-5)

:::note[Guidance]
For passwords, [NIST SP 800-63B-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) (July 2025) says verifiers shall not require periodic changes, and shall force a change when there is evidence of compromise. Set the change periods below by authenticator type, and keep scheduled changes for secrets such as shared or service account keys.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service or device receiving an authenticator as part of its initial distribution. (IA-5a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall establish the initial content of any authenticator the organization issues. (IA-5b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use. (IA-5c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost, compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators. (IA-5d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall implement those procedures. (IA-5d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure default authenticators are changed before first use. (IA-5e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall change or refresh authenticators as follows: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: a time period for changing or refreshing authenticators by authenticator type <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: no scheduled change for user passwords; certificates at expiry; shared and service account secrets at least annually</span></span>. (IA-5f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall change or refresh authenticators when <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that trigger the change or refreshment of authenticators <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: evidence or suspicion of compromise, and departure of a person who knew a shared authenticator</span></span> occur. (IA-5f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification. (IA-5g)
- Users shall protect their authenticators as the rules of behavior require. (IA-5h)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure devices implement the controls that protect authenticators. (IA-5h)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall change the authenticators of group or role accounts when membership of those accounts changes. (IA-5i)

#### Password-based authentication (IA-5(1))

:::note[Guidance]
The typical values follow [NIST SP 800-63B-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) (July 2025): a minimum of 15 characters for a password used alone and 8 when it is one factor of several, no other composition rules, at least 64 characters allowed, and a check against a list of common and breached passwords.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall maintain a list of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords, and update it <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to update the list of commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least monthly, and whenever a relevant breach corpus is published</span></span> and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised. (IA-5(1)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system verifies, when users create or update passwords, that the passwords are not on that list. (IA-5(1)(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure passwords are transmitted only over cryptographically protected channels. (IA-5(1)(c))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure passwords are stored using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash. (IA-5(1)(d))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system requires immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery. (IA-5(1)(e))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system allows long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters. (IA-5(1)(f))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ automated tools to help users select strong passwords. (IA-5(1)(g))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system enforces these composition and complexity rules: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: authenticator composition and complexity rules <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a minimum length of 15 characters for passwords used as the only factor and 8 for passwords used with another factor, and no other composition rules</span></span>. (IA-5(1)(h))

#### Public key-based authentication (IA-5(2))

- For public key-based authentication, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system enforces authorized access to the corresponding private key. (IA-5(2)(a)(1))
- For public key-based authentication, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system maps the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group. (IA-5(2)(a)(2))
- When public key infrastructure is used, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system validates certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status. (IA-5(2)(b)(1))
- When public key infrastructure is used, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system keeps a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation. (IA-5(2)(b)(2))

#### Protection of authenticators (IA-5(6))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information that their use gives access to. (IA-5(6))

#### Authentication feedback (IA-6)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system obscures feedback of authentication information during authentication, so it cannot be exploited by unauthorized individuals. (IA-6)

#### Cryptographic module authentication (IA-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards and guidelines that apply to such authentication. (IA-7)

#### Identification and authentication (non-organizational users) (IA-8)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system uniquely identifies and authenticates non-organizational users and processes acting on their behalf. (IA-8)

#### Acceptance of PIV credentials from other agencies (IA-8(1))

:::note[Guidance]
This enhancement applies where federal employees or contractors from other agencies use the system. Outside that case, record it as not applicable in the system security plan with that reason.
:::

- Where users from federal agencies access the system, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure it accepts and electronically verifies their Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials. (IA-8(1))

#### Acceptance of external authenticators (IA-8(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system accepts only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, such as those meeting [NIST SP 800-63B-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) (July 2025). (IA-8(2)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators. (IA-8(2)(b))

#### Use of defined profiles (IA-8(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system conforms to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: identity management profiles <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the federation profiles the organization publishes for its identity provider, such as SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect</span></span> for identity management. (IA-8(4))

#### Re-authentication (IA-11)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system requires users to re-authenticate when <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: circumstances or situations requiring re-authentication <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a session timeout, a change of role or privilege, a privileged action, or a change of authenticators</span></span>. (IA-11)

#### Identity proofing (IA-12)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall identity proof users who require accounts for logical access, at the identity assurance level the applicable standards require, such as the NIST SP 800-63-4 digital identity guidelines. (IA-12a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall resolve each user identity to a unique individual. (IA-12b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall collect, validate and verify identity evidence. (IA-12c)

#### Identity evidence (IA-12(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall require evidence of individual identification to be presented to the registration authority. (IA-12(2))

#### Identity evidence validation and verification (IA-12(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall require presented identity evidence to be validated and verified through <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: methods of validation and verification of identity evidence <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: checking the evidence against its issuing or an authoritative source, and confirming the applicant is the person it describes</span></span>. (IA-12(3))

#### Address confirmation (IA-12(5))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall require a <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one: registration code; notice of proofing <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: registration code</span></span> to be delivered through an out-of-band channel to verify the user's address of record, physical or digital. (IA-12(5))

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current identification and authentication policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current identification and authentication policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (IA-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current identification and authentication procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require identification and authentication procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (IA-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (IA-1a.1(b))

</div>
